description.value: An fMRI study examining neural responses to smoking-ritual stimuli at four stages in nonsmokers, nondeprived smokers, and deprived smokers.

spans.text: This fMRI study compared 20 nondeprived smokers with 20 nonsmokers to unravel the influence of smoking-related pictures displaying the beginning (BEGIN-stimuli) and termination (END-stimuli) of the smoking ritual on neural activity in the addiction network.

value: for nondeprived and deprived smokers, we hypothesized that BEGIN-stimuli lead to neuronal activations, whereas END-stimuli should result in deactivations.
We expected that these effects are significantly different between nondeprived smokers and nonsmokers.

description.value: Three participant groups were studied: nonsmokers, nondeprived smokers, and deprived smokers. Smokers were randomly assigned to the nondeprived or deprived group; deprived smokers underwent at least 12 hours of deprivation.

spans.text: In all, 60 right-handed subjects participated in the study: 20 nondeprived smokers (11 female), 20 deprived smokers (10 female), and 20 nonsmokers (10 female).
